task: Task 2 — Mnemonik MCP role npm rewrite + binary discovery
summary: Clean, well-scoped rewrite. The binary discovery cascade, supply-chain double-pin (npm ci + global install), MCP-stdio smoke handshake, and all 8 contract tests are correctly implemented. Three minor issues found: a silent no-op path when mnemonic_mcp_enabled=false leaves mnemonic_mcp_binary undefined for downstream consumers; an idempotency gap in the npm ci step; and a potential `which` ambiguity on a VM with a stale descoped binary.

issues.title: mnemonic_mcp_binary fact is never set when mnemonic_mcp_enabled=false — downstream Task 3 silently fails with UndefinedError
issues.description:
The entire install block is guarded with `when: mnemonic_mcp_enabled | bool`. When this is false, the `set_fact: mnemonic_mcp_binary` task on line 117-118 is skipped, leaving `mnemonic_mcp_binary` undefined. The content-publisher role (Task 3) uses `{{ mnemonic_mcp_binary }}` in `blogger.mcp.json.j2` without a default, so if an operator disables the MCP role (e.g. rolling back) and redeploys, the content-publisher role will fail at template render with a Jinja `UndefinedError` on `mnemonic_mcp_binary`.

Although `mnemonic_mcp_enabled` is now `true` by default, the existing deploy.yml comment on lines 248-255 explicitly anticipates operators disabling this role. The contract test `test_tasks_set_fact_for_binary_discovery` doesn't test the disabled-path.
issues.recommendation:
Add a fallback set_fact outside the `when` block that sets `mnemonic_mcp_binary` to an empty string or sentinel when the role is disabled:

- name: Set mnemonic_mcp_binary to empty sentinel when MCP is disabled
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    mnemonic_mcp_binary: ""
  when: not (mnemonic_mcp_enabled | bool)

This makes the downstream failure in blogger.mcp.json.j2 explicit (empty command field) rather than a cryptic UndefinedError. Alternatively, add `| default('')` to the `{{ mnemonic_mcp_binary }}` reference in Task 3's template, but that silently produces a broken JSON config. The set_fact fallback is more correct.
issues.impact: If an operator ever flips mnemonic_mcp_enabled=false and redeploys the full playbook, the content-publisher role fails with an opaque UndefinedError mid-play. Not a current production risk (enabled=true), but breaks the fail-loud contract that the role explicitly advertises.

issues.title: npm ci idempotency: always reruns even when lockfile is unchanged
issues.description:
The `npm ci` task (lines 86-91) has `changed_when: mnemonik_npm_ci.rc == 0 and 'up to date' not in (mnemonik_npm_ci.stdout | default(''))`. However, `npm ci` always performs a clean install (it deletes and reinstalls `node_modules`) — it never prints 'up to date'. This means the task is always marked `changed` on every playbook run, which: (1) makes Ansible diffs noisy (operators can't distinguish actual changes from re-runs), and (2) triggers unnecessary reinstalls on every deploy, adding 10-30s to the play.

The lockfile copy task does register `mnemonik_lockfile_copy`, but the npm ci task doesn't condition on `mnemonik_lockfile_copy.changed`.
issues.recommendation:
Gate npm ci on lockfile change:
  when: mnemonik_lockfile_copy.changed

This makes the step truly idempotent: if the checked-in lockfile hasn't changed (most redeploys), npm ci is skipped. If the lockfile was updated (version bump), npm ci runs. The global install step after it already has `state: present` idempotency via community.general.npm.
issues.impact: Extra ~10-30s on every deploy and noisy changed status in Ansible output. No correctness issue.

issues.title: which cascade may resolve stale descoped binary from /opt/mnemonic-mcp/bin/ if it's on PATH
issues.description:
The task spec (Details, Edge cases) acknowledges that the old descoped install may have left `/opt/mnemonic-mcp/bin/mnemonic-mcp` on the VM. If that directory is on PATH (e.g. from the previous role's Environment= in the systemd unit or from a leftover /etc/profile.d/ snippet), the `which mnemonic-mcp` fallback in the cascade will resolve to the OLD binary, not the newly npm-installed one. The `mnemonic_mcp_binary` fact would then point at a stale binary, and the systemd unit would launch the wrong process.

The task spec says this cleanup is 'optional' — but without it, the discovery is not trustworthy on VMs that ran the old role.
issues.recommendation:
Add an explicit cleanup task before the discovery step:

- name: Remove stale descoped binary to prevent which ambiguity
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: /opt/mnemonic-mcp/bin/mnemonic-mcp
    state: absent
  failed_when: false

Alternatively, use `npm bin -g` or `npm root -g` to construct the expected binary path deterministically rather than relying on PATH-based discovery. This is more robust and eliminates the ambiguity entirely.
issues.impact: On a VM that previously ran the descoped role, the service would launch the OLD (non-MCP-stdio) binary. The smoke handshake at the end of the role would catch this — it would fail — but the failure message would be confusing since the binary path in the fact would look correct.

positive_observations: The two-layer supply-chain pin (npm ci from lockfile for transitive tree + community.general.npm for global binary placement) is well-designed and matches the task spec's R2-8 requirement. The separation of concerns is clear.

The MCP-stdio initialize handshake smoke test is correct and complete: JSON-RPC payload via stdin (nothing in argv), head -1 for the response, python3 inline parser asserting protocolVersion in result. This exactly matches Decision 3 + Architecture step 4.
The binary name is in `set_fact` without `cacheable: true` — correct for same-play fact propagation to Task 3. The README fact-propagation section explains this clearly.
test_no_sign_memory_anywhere is an excellent regression guard. It's a pattern that should be replicated for other 'this subcommand does not exist' invariants.

The `.ansible-lint` config skip list is minimal and each skip is documented with a rationale. The `role-name` skip is repo-wide consistent; the molecule/converge.yml exclusion is accurate (molecule isn't wired into CI).

All descoped artifacts are cleanly removed: templates/config.yml.j2, templates/protocol-qa.env.j2, templates/molyanov-mnemonic-hooks.yml.j2, templates/hooks/. The templates/ directory now contains only the one file it should.

The systemd unit hardening block is comprehensive — it goes well beyond what the spec required (CapabilityBoundingSet=, MemoryDenyWriteExecute=, ProtectKernelTunables= etc). LimitCORE= is not present (not required for this role), and the added UMask=0077 is appropriate.

The bump runbook in README correctly includes: regenerate lockfile offline, strict-pin the root dep, update defaults, commit + deploy, post-deploy sanity with doctor. The third-binary-spelling edge case is documented with the npm list -g alternative.
The Node.js prerequisite block correctly guards against re-running NodeSource setup when node is already present, avoiding unnecessary APT source modifications on existing VMs.

The README's 'What it does NOT install' section is valuable — it explicitly documents the Vaultwarden signing-key removal and the sign-memory absence, which prevents future contributors from re-introducing those paths.
